newsitem.title: USA: Tropical Storm Ana forms off North Carolina coast.
newsitem.headline: Tropical Storm Ana forms off North Carolina coast.

text.p: The first tropical storm of the one-month-old Atlantic hurricane season churned off the North Carolina coast on Tuesday but posed no immediate threat to land as it moved slowly off to sea, the National Hurricane Center said.

At 5:00 p.m. EDT 2100 GMT, the center of Tropical Storm Ana was located about 300 miles (490 km) south-southeast of Hatteras, North Carolina, and was moving east near 10 mph (17 kph), forecasters said.
The system formed Monday evening as a tropical depression. Tropical depressions become tropical storms when maximum sustained winds reach 39 mph (63 kph).

Ana's maximum sustained winds were near 45 mph (75 kph), and extended outward up to 115 miles (185 km) from its center. Little change in strength was forecast through Wednesday evening, and the system was expected to turn toward the northeast, a track that would move it even further from the U.S. coast.
Ana would become a hurricane if its maximum sustained winds reached 74 mph (119 kph). The six-month Atlantic hurricane season begins June 1 and ends Nov. 30.
